items.title: Water is densest at 4 degrees Celsius, not zero
items.claim: Cool any substance and it gets denser as it approaches freezing — except water. Water reaches maximum density at 4 degrees Celsius and then becomes LESS dense as it cools further to 0 degrees Celsius.
items.prompt: Why does ice float on liquid water?

options.text: Trapped air bubbles make ice less dense than liquid water
Hydrogen bonds force water molecules into an open hexagonal lattice on freezing, so solid water occupies about 9 percent more volume than liquid water
Ice is colder, and colder things float
Surface tension on the underside of ice holds it up

items.reveal_title: Hydrogen bonding wins over packing efficiency
items.reveal:
In liquid water, hydrogen bonds break and re-form constantly, and molecules can crowd together. When water freezes, every molecule locks into a tetrahedral arrangement where each oxygen hydrogen-bonds to exactly four neighbours. That structure is open and roomy — about 9 percent more volume than the liquid.

This is why ponds freeze top-down rather than bottom-up. Fish survive winter because the densest water (4 degrees Celsius) sinks and the ice layer insulates everything below. If water behaved normally, lakes would freeze solid and life as we know it could not exist.
items.why: Students assume cooling always increases density. The hydrogen bond's geometry, not the temperature, controls the packing.

items.title: Oxygen exists as a molecule with TWO unpaired electrons
items.claim: O2 is a closed-shell, even-electron molecule. By the textbook Lewis structure (O=O), all electrons are paired. Yet liquid oxygen is magnetic — drip it between the poles of a strong magnet and it sticks.

options.text: Liquid O2 contains impurities of iron
Molecular orbital theory shows O2's highest occupied orbitals are two degenerate pi-antibonding orbitals, each holding ONE electron — by Hund's rule, both are unpaired
Liquid O2 is actually O3 in disguise
Magnetic fields ionise O2 into charged species

items.reveal_title: Lewis dot structures don't capture orbital occupancy
items.reveal:
Build O2's MO diagram: combine atomic orbitals of two oxygens. Filling 16 electrons in order gives a configuration ending with (pi*) squared — but the two pi-antibonding orbitals are degenerate, and by Hund's rule each gets one electron with parallel spins.

The molecule has bond order 2 (matches O=O) but it also has 2 unpaired electrons (does not match O=O). Lewis structures are a useful shorthand but they hide quantum mechanical detail.

Videos of liquid oxygen being held in place between magnet poles are striking — the same thing that lets O2 carry around our blood is the same thing that holds it to a magnet.
items.why: Lewis structures count electrons in pairs and tell you nothing about magnetism. Molecular orbital theory does — and is correct.

items.title: The element you breathe and the element that protects you are the same element
items.claim: Atmospheric oxygen is O2 — diatomic, paramagnetic, essential for respiration. Ozone is O3 — pale blue, pungent, toxic at ground level, and shields the planet from UV. Both are pure oxygen.
items.prompt: Why do ozone and oxygen behave so differently?

options.text: Ozone contains a heavier isotope of oxygen
Three-atom O3 has a bent structure with delocalised pi bonding that absorbs UV strongly (200-310 nm); two-atom O2 has different MO energies and no comparable absorption
The two are not the same element after all

items.reveal:
Ozone is bent (about 117 degrees) with three resonance structures and bond order 1.5 per O-O bond. Its electronic transitions absorb the Hartley band (200-310 nm) strongly — almost all the Sun's biologically damaging UV-B and UV-C.

This is why the Montreal Protocol (1987) was such an unusually successful environmental treaty: CFCs were depleting stratospheric ozone, and replacing them has allowed the ozone layer to begin to recover.

Ground-level ozone produced by photochemical smog is toxic to lungs at parts-per-billion. Same molecule, life-saving at 30 km up, lung-damaging at the surface.
items.why: Allotropes of an element are not minor variants. They can be biologically and atmospherically opposite.
